newsitem.title: USA: IMM currency futures end up mostly in quiet day.
newsitem.headline: IMM currency futures end up mostly in quiet day.

text.p: IMM currency futures ended mostly up in a slack session ahead of key U.S. jobs data Friday.
With the dollar sidelined to tight ranges Thursday, most currency futures also stayed confined to familiar territory.

June yen futures were firm all session, and managed to extend overnight gains as high as $0.008674 on lingering ideas Japan was due for an interest rate hike. But overall, trade was noncommittal ahead of the May jobs report.
A Reuters poll of economists showed an average estimate for May jobs up 219,000 and a jobless rate of 5.0 percent.
In the previous report, jobs grew 142,000 and the unemployment rate fell to 4.9 percent.
The latest weekly jobless claims early Thursday gave little impetus to currency futures. Claims in the latest week rose an unexpected 19,000 to 337,000.
While continental currencies remained tethered to tight ranges, Mexican peso futures saw aggressive selling pressure.
One trader said "major selling" hit the market amid pre-election jitters and dollar bullishness.
"From what I'm hearing, they're bailing out of pesos and into the dollar," the trader said.
He pegged June peso support at $0.124700 and $0.124200.
Another trader, Rogelio Larrinaga, assistant vice president with Sakura Dellsher's Latin America desk, said peso trade was quiet early, but turned very heavy on the close.
He said early illiquidity hampered the market when selling pressure emerged midday. He noted sell-stop orders at $0.125000 and $0.125100.
"It was very crazy on the close," he said. He too cited "a little bit of uncertainty" before July 6 congressional elections and selling pesos for dollars.
Traders noted that September currency contracts will take lead status on Monday, with rolling activity out of June expected all next week.

At the close, June yen was up $0.000045 at $0.008661, marks rose $0.0006 to $0.5787, Swiss francs rose $0.0003 to $0.6923, sterling was up $0.0014 at $1.6330, Can dollars were down $0.0009 to $0.7269, Aussie dollars were up $0.0028 to $0.7607, and Mexican pesos were $0.000725 lower at $0.124800.
